How do they differ from bacteria? 3.2.1 GENERAL INTRODUCTION Viruses are ultramicroscopic intracellular parasites, which consist of a single nucleic acid, either DNAor RNA covered with a protein coat called capsid. Viruses do not consist of cellular organization. These are acellular pathogens. Hence, they are neither prokaryotes nor eukaryotes. Viruses crystalize like non-living things (chemicals) outside the host cell but show only living characteristics that is they replicate only inside the host cell. So, they are considered midway/borderline between the living and nonliving things. They may even be purified and crystallized like chemical substances. Viruses are completely devoid of the machinery for life processes so it requires the presence of host cell for its multiplication/replication. As they compulsorily need host cells to replicate or show their living characteristics, it is considered an obligatory parasite. In five kingdom classification of Whittaker virus doesn’t get any defined place. A newly formed complete infectious virus particle is called virion.
